chunks: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isam (mercy of God be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni said: 'Ali ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Tamimi, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwan, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him), who said: I asked my father, the Master of the Worshippers (peace be upon him)

I said to him: O father! Inform me about when our grandfather the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ascended to the heaven and his Lord commanded him with fifty prayers, why did he not ask for relief for his Ummah until Musa ibn 'Imran (peace be upon him) said to him: Return to your Lord and ask for relief, for your Ummah cannot bear that?

He (peace be upon him) answered: O son! Verily, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not suggest anything to his Lord, nor reconsider anything He commanded him to. When Musa (peace be upon him) asked him that and became an intercessor for his Ummah to him, it was not permissible for him to reject the intercession of his brother Musa (peace be upon him). So he returned to his Lord and asked for relief until it was reduced to five prayers.
He said: I then asked: O father! Then why did he not return to his Lord and ask for relief after the five prayers?

He replied: O son! He intended that his Ummah obtain relief along with the reward of fifty prayers, based on the word of Allah: 'Whoever brings a good deed, he shall have ten like it.' Do you not see that when he descended to the earth, Jibril (peace be upon him) revealed to him saying: O Muhammad, your Lord sends you greetings and says: They are five for fifty. 'My word shall not be changed, nor am I unjust to the servants.'
He said: I asked him: O father! Is it not that Allah, the Exalted, is not described by place?
He said: Yes, exalted is Allah from that. I said: Then what is the meaning of Musa's (peace be upon him) word to the Messenger of Allah: 'Return to your Lord'?

He said: Its meaning is the meaning of Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) word: 'Surely I fly to my Lord; He will guide me.' And the meaning of Musa's (peace be upon him) word: 'And I hastened on to Thee, my Lord, that Thou might be pleased.' And the meaning of the Mighty and High's word: 'Therefore fly to Allah,' which means 'Pilgrimage to the House of Allah.' O son! Verily, the Ka'bah is the House of Allah; whoever makes pilgrimage to the House of Allah has endeavored to reach Allah. The mosques are the Houses of Allah; whoever proceeds to them has proceeded to Allah and endeavored to visit Him. The praying person, as long as he is in his prayer, is standing before Allah, Lofty be His Majesty.

The people of the stand of 'Arafat are standing before Allah, the Mighty and High. Verily, for Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, are places in His heavens; whoever is ascended to them is ascended to Him. Do you not hear Allah saying: 'To Him ascend the angels and the Spirit'? And He says: 'To Him do ascend the good words and the good deeds lift them up.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Prophet Muhammad not ask for more than five prayers during Mi'raj and what is the meaning of 'returning to the Lord'?
ai.summary: Zayd ibn 'Ali elucidates the theological nuance of the Mi'raj, noting that the Prophet’s acceptance of five prayers with fifty rewards reflects a divine mercy ensuring both ease and full recompense for the Ummah. He further clarifies that 'returning to the Lord' (ruju' ila Rabbika) denotes spiritual ascent and proximity rather than physical movement, aligning with the Shia doctrine of Allah's transcendence beyond space and direction. This interpretation underscores that mosques, the Ka'bah, and the state of prayer are all valid means of connecting to the Divine, who is not confined to a specific location.
